title: Gen 7 · phase 2: volume (30% fast self-play, 30% standard self-play, 20% standard v Gen 6, 5% each of four anchors)
pending: Phase 1 first: this plan opens when every phase 1 pair has 2,000 completed boards.

Self-play pairs (7f-32~7f-32, 7s-32~7s-32) need a runtime with the self-play regime. The collectors' branches have it; this branch, like `main` at b0909bb, validates common and native only. The engine files of this branch have to be carried onto that runtime, as a new source identity.
notes: Not open yet: `launch_enabled` is false and `pending` is not empty, so ops/prepare_gen7_alpha.py refuses this file. Max accepted Gen 7 and set the standard bot's tree on 12 November 2026 (margin 0.25, trust 0.3, `path` 0.5, 3 tricks); what remains is in `pending`.
A Gen 7 bot is its Gen 6 base bot (same bidder, lead net, scorer, layouts and sample count) with the gen7 engine and policy v4. docs/gen7_alpha_2026-11-11.md explains every setting.

Audit and capture settings (tie audits, gap forks, room seeds) are carried over from the source run, not set here. BEN boards carry no audits (`ben_audit`). Gen 5 and Gen 1 boards carry the cohort's: there is no per-pair switch.
Weights are twentieths of the boards: 6, 6, 4, 1, 1, 1, 1. A self-play board is one table; a two-bot board is two tables on one deal, so in tables the two-bot pairs weigh double.
Self-play supplies training data and has no IMP comparison, as for Gen 6.
